title: Dedicated capacity: surge shaping and locality tagging for regional/multi-zone fleets
creator: Miguel Torres
description:
Summary:
Implement a combined set of placement and runtime controls for Dedicated regional and multi-zone fleets that (1) guarantee committed throughput under typical operating conditions, (2) shape short-term surge traffic to avoid noisy neighbors and unacceptable latency variance, and (3) enforce customer data locality constraints via locality tags rather than brittle hard-residency locks.

Goals:
- Provide customer-visible throughput guarantees (hedging) at the pool level while enabling autoscaling and burst behavior.
- Prevent cross-region or cross-zone placements that violate explicit locality constraints and surface clear fallbacks when constraints cannot be met.
- Introduce a lightweight "locality tag" model for placement; these tags are respected by the placement engine and appear on allocation metadata and billing dashboards.
- Implement surge-shaping algorithms (short-window rate smoothing + admission control) to both preserve latency SLOs and avoid capacity collapse when neighboring tenants spike.

Technical approach (high level):
- Tag model: add a locality_tag string to pool configs (e.g., "eu:fr", "na:us-west-2", "ap:sg"). Tags are soft by default (preference) and can be set to strict to require enforcement.
- Hedging/throughput guarantees: implement a capacity hedging layer that reserves a percentage of committed pool capacity for guaranteed throughput; use token-bucket accounting at routing time to honor committed throughput while allowing controlled burst consumption against pooled burst capacity.
- Surge shaping: admission controller sits before batching queue; it applies short-window smoothing and backpressure to clients (429 or queued streaming) when the instant load threatens latency targets. Shape parameters (window, smoothing factor, max-queue) are per-pool and tunable via the Dedicated Console.
- Failover behavior: when locality_tag cannot be satisfied, routing evaluates fallback policies in order: (1) strict -> fail request / return configured error, (2) preference -> route to next-best pool with an annotated residency breach event, (3) emergency -> route to fallback pool in another region but mark tokens as cross-region for billing and compliance audit.
- Placement engine changes: matching algorithm extended to prefer exact tag matches then prefer same-region pools, then cross-region candidates per fallback policy. Scheduling will also consider existing KV-cache locality and warm replicas to reduce cold-start latency for failovers.

Why not hard locks only:
Hard residency locks (always preferred in some previous proposals) increase fragmentation and make autoscaling and burst inefficient. The locality tag model aims to balance compliance requirements with practical throughput economics by allowing customers to opt into strict mode when necessary and otherwise use preference mode for improved capacity utilization.

Metrics/KPIs:
- Committed throughput SLO: 99.95% of committed units delivered within pool latency SLO under normal load.
- Failover RTO target: 30s median for routing to fallback pool with warm replicas, 120s worst-case for cold-start paths.
- Latency penalty under surge shaping: <15% p99 increase compared to steady-state.
- Telemetry: surface residency-breach events, hedged-capacity consumption, admission-control throttles in Console.

Acceptance criteria:
- Routing honors locality_tag strict/preference semantics for new fleet configs.
- Hedging tokens implemented and can be observed per pool; committed throughput can be simulated in integration tests.
- Surge shaping admission controller prevents >10% p99 latency spikes in synthetic burst tests while preserving at least 90% of committed throughput.
- Console shows locality tags, hedged vs. burst consumption, and residency-breach events on per-pool dashboard.
- Documentation and public API: SDK and REST examples updated; customers can set locality_tag and hedging percentage.

Rollout plan (phases):
1) Internal canary within staging: enable preference tags only, monitor hedging metrics and telemetry.
2) Beta with select customers: expose strict mode behind feature flag, collect compliance feedback.
3) General availability: UI controls in Console, SDK docs, release notes.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Overly-conservative hedging reduces capacity for bursts. Mitigation: default hedging set low (5-10%) with recommended tuning guidance.
- Risk: Customers misunderstand soft vs strict semantics. Mitigation: clear Console UI and warning banners; telemetry and test tools in Console to simulate placement outcomes.
- Risk: Complexity in placement engine increases scheduling latency. Mitigation: incremental rollout and benchmarks; caching of tag-match results and warm-replica heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Locality tags (preference and strict) honored by placement engine and visible in pool metadata
Hedged token accounting implemented; metrics emitted for hedged vs burst consumption
